about: Rename map for the word 'etzhayyim' in awai / itonami / kotoba. Owner decisions 2026-11-04 (JUN-842): (1) targets follow where the thing is defined: kotoba-lang repositories -> org.kotoba-lang, awai network repositories (network-awai, cloud-itonami) -> network.awai; (2) did:web is not kept, new identities are did:webvh; (3) no compatibility period, one cut-over; (4) serving old URLs / contexts / redirects is optional. Rules are tried in order; the first whose `match` (case-insensitive regex on one token) hits classifies the token. `status`: keep = never rename; apply = rewrite with the code that uses it; mint = the new value is created, not derived by pattern (did:webvh); lookup = target comes from a table; decide = owner decision per case. `to` may contain {nsid} {wit} {domain} {npm}, filled from `targets` by the owner org: for lexicon NSIDs the owner is the repository that defines the lexicon (a lexicon id is global, so a user in another repository gets the same new id), otherwise the repository the token is found in.

rules.note: Mint a did:webvh for the service (the SCID comes from the first log entry, so it cannot be derived by pattern); the host changes to the new domain. The old did:web document need not be served.

rules.kind: DID used as an entity identifier (did:web:etzhayyim.com:actor:..., :gov:...)
rules.note: About 26 thousand distinct values, mostly data identifiers (actor:*, gov:*), not key holders. P1 step 1: find which are resolved as DID documents; those get a did:webvh, the rest are rewritten to another identifier scheme.
Another DID method (did:etzhayyim:...); decide whether to mint did:webvh instead, like did:web.
Content / record identifiers (news items, ...) stored in data; with one cut-over they would be rewritten with the data. Owner decision on the new URN namespace.
Package / repository names ending in the word; follows the repo-path lookup.
Wire protocol: accept both names for a window, then drop (alias).
Not covered by the awai.network / kotoba-lang.org proposal.
Deployment configuration; renaming breaks running deployments until both are set.
Class / function names: rename with their callers in one change (P1).
Always owned by kotoba-lang. One cut-over, no dual accept.
Owner = the repository that defines the lexicon.
Owner = the repository that defines the lexicon (table built by the tool from lexicon JSON files).
Library packages may still prefer kotoba:* (decide per package).

rules.blocker: The new URL must answer before the cut-over; the old one need not be served.
New names need DNS and certificates before the cut-over; redirects from the old names are optional.

rules.note: Appears as ids, at:// handles and vanity names; depends on the two rules above.

rules.blocker: The target scope must exist and be owned. For network-awai / cloud-itonami no scope is decided yet: those tokens stay decide.

rules.note: Target is the repository's current home (for example network-awai/actor-X); needs a table, not a pattern.

Fragments of hosts / handles / paths; follows the vanity-url and host decisions.
